question.text: Which musician released the song 'Let's Dance'?

results.hint: Chic's Nile Rodgers co-produced the song.
results.explanation: David Bowie recorded the song with producer Nile Rodgers, whose work with Chic helped bring a dance-oriented sound to Bowie's album of the same name.

question.text: Which German rock band released the song 'Rock You Like a Hurricane'?

results.hint: The same band is known for power ballads such as “Wind of Change” and “Still Loving You.”
results.explanation: Scorpions released the song on their 1984 album Love at First Sting, and it became one of the band’s signature hard-rock anthems.

question.text: What is a recurring theme in a musical or literary work called?

results.hint: It can be a repeated image, object, or phrase that gains significance as a work unfolds.
results.explanation: A motif can be a recurring pattern of notes, images, or ideas. A chorus and verse are song sections, while a melody is a sequence of notes.

question.text: What do people mean when type the letters 'FTW' in a message on the internet?

results.hint: It often follows a favorite choice or idea as an enthusiastic endorsement.
results.explanation: For The Win is a celebratory expression used to endorse something or call it excellent, echoing a sports-style shout of victory.

question.text: Which DC Comics supervillain is a menace to Batman?

results.hint: His scaly skin and powerful jaws give him a distinctly reptilian appearance.
results.explanation: Killer Croc was born Waylon Jones and developed a reptilian appearance that made him an imposing Batman foe.

question.text: Which actress has played roles in both X-Men: Days of Future Past and Die Another Day?

results.hint: She also played the title character in the superhero film Catwoman.
results.explanation: Halle Berry also played NSA agent Jinx in Die Another Day, a James Bond film.

question.text: What is the name for a piece of glass that separates light into the visible spectrum?

results.hint: Newton famously used one to show that white light contains a range of colors.
results.explanation: A prism bends different wavelengths of light by different amounts, separating white light into its component colors.

question.text: What plant's oil, called urushiol, causes skin irritation when it comes into contact with human skin?

results.hint: A well-known plant is summed up by the saying 'leaves of three, let it be'.
results.explanation: Urushiol, the oily resin of poison ivy, triggers an allergic rash on contact with skin.

question.text: Which Irish rock band released the single 'Zombie'?

results.hint: Dolores O'Riordan was the band's distinctive lead singer.
results.explanation: The Cranberries’ song was written in response to the 1993 Warrington bombings in England.

question.text: What is the name of the highest mountain in Japan?

results.hint: Its nearly symmetrical volcanic cone is an iconic landmark visible from Tokyo on clear days.
results.explanation: Mount Fuji is an active volcano whose most recent recorded eruption was in 1707.

question.text: Which author wrote 'The Hunchback of Notre Dame'?

results.hint: The same French novelist also wrote Les Misérables.
results.explanation: Victor Hugo's novel was originally published in French as Notre-Dame de Paris; its English title highlights the bell-ringer Quasimodo.

question.text: Which material do paper wasps chew to build their nests?

results.hint: Their nests have a papery texture, made from pulp scraped from weathered outdoor surfaces.
results.explanation: Paper wasps mix wood fibers with saliva to make a lightweight pulp that dries into the nest’s walls.

question.text: Who assassinated president Kennedy?

results.hint: The former Marine was arrested in Dallas shortly after the shooting.
results.explanation: Lee Harvey Oswald was arrested in Dallas, but Jack Ruby shot him two days later while he was being transferred, so he never stood trial.

question.text: Which of these countries is the most populous?

results.hint: Its population surpassed China's in 2023, making it the world's most populous country.
results.explanation: India became the world's most populous country in 2023, ahead of China; the United States and Indonesia also have smaller populations.

question.text: Which high-protein grain, related to spinach, was known as the "gold of the Incas"?

results.hint: Its cultivation was centered in the Andes, where it was a staple crop long before Europeans arrived.
results.explanation: Quinoa is technically a pseudocereal: it is a seed used like a grain, rather than a true cereal grain.

question.text: Which piece of written work starts with the line 'Among other public buildings in a certain town, which for many reasons it will be prudent to refrain from mentioning, and to which I will assign no fictitious name, there is one anciently common to most towns, great or small: to wit, a workhouse; and in this workhouse was born; on a day and date which I need not trouble myself to repeat, inasmuch as it can be of no possible consequence to the'?

results.hint: Charles Dickens wrote this Victorian novel about a boy born in a workhouse.
results.explanation: Oliver Twist is one of Dickens's best-known novels; its orphan protagonist's request for more food became one of the story's most famous scenes.

question.text: Which spacecraft carried Yuri Gagarin on the first crewed spaceflight in 1961?

results.hint: The single-person capsule completed one orbit of Earth during the historic flight.
results.explanation: Vostok 1 completed one orbit of Earth, making Gagarin the first human to travel into space.

question.text: Which actress has starred in both The Silence of the Lambs and Taxi Driver?

results.hint: She won Academy Awards for The Accused and The Silence of the Lambs.
results.explanation: Jodie Foster won the Academy Award for Best Actress for playing Clarice Starling in The Silence of the Lambs.

question.text: Which explorer is best known for exploring and surveying North America's northwest Pacific coast regions?

results.hint: The large island off British Columbia’s coast was named in his honor.
results.explanation: Captain Vancouver commanded the expedition aboard HMS Discovery that charted much of the coast. Vancouver Island and the city of Vancouver later took his name.

question.text: What is the plot of the movie The Prestige?

results.hint: Hugh Jackman and Christian Bale face off in this Christopher Nolan period drama.
results.explanation: The Prestige follows two rival stage conjurers in Victorian London whose competition escalates as each tries to outdo the other with an apparently impossible act.

question.text: Which country is Stilton cheese from?

results.hint: Its namesake village is in Cambridgeshire, near Peterborough.
results.explanation: England’s Stilton is named after a Cambridgeshire village, but traditional Stilton cheese is produced in Derbyshire, Leicestershire, and Nottinghamshire.

question.text: What were the fortified roadside inns that sheltered Silk Road merchants and their camels called?

results.hint: They often had a central courtyard surrounded by rooms and stables.
results.explanation: Caravanserais commonly placed rooms and stables around an enclosed courtyard, giving travelers and their animals a secure place to rest.

question.text: In which athletics event did Colin Jackson set a world record in 1993?

results.hint: The race involves sprinting over ten evenly spaced barriers.
results.explanation: Jackson ran 12.91 seconds at the 1993 World Championships in Stuttgart, and the mark remained the world record for 13 years.

question.text: What type of wine is Beaujolais Nouveau?

results.hint: Its Gamay grapes have dark skins that tint the wine during fermentation.
results.explanation: Red Beaujolais Nouveau is made mainly from Gamay grapes and is released soon after harvest, so it is meant to be enjoyed young.

question.text: Which region of the human skull includes the zygomatic bones and the vomer?

results.hint: It forms the face.
results.explanation: The zygomatic and vomer are facial bones, part of the facial skeleton.

question.text: Which novel by Louis Sachar begins with the line 'There is no lake at Camp Green Lake'?

results.hint: The title refers to what the boys dig.
results.explanation: Holes by Louis Sachar opens with the line 'There is no lake at Camp Green Lake', and won the 1999 Newbery Medal.

question.text: Which Mexican commemoration celebrates Mexico's victory over France at the Battle of Puebla?

results.hint: The date is in its name.
results.explanation: Cinco de Mayo marks the Mexican army's 1862 victory over France at the Battle of Puebla.

question.text: In which city did Mother Teresa establish the Missionaries of Charity?

results.hint: This eastern Indian metropolis lies on the Hooghly River and was once the capital of British India.
results.explanation: Calcutta became the Missionaries of Charity’s founding base in 1950; the order is known for serving people in poverty.

question.text: Which author wrote 'The Stand'?

results.hint: Carrie and It are among this horror novelist's best-known books.
results.explanation: Stephen King's post-apocalyptic novel follows survivors of a devastating pandemic and their struggle between good and evil.

question.text: What do we measure in Hertz?

results.hint: A wave’s number of cycles per second is expressed in this unit.
results.explanation: Hertz measures frequency: one hertz is one cycle per second. The unit is named for physicist Heinrich Hertz.
